elimination.downtown_copper_pot: Only lamb, chicken or beef curries; plain rice for a non-meat eater. Fails Mina's diet (deal-breaker).
elimination.downtown_cardamom_house: Vegetarian options and fast, but $$ and reviewed as a treat-yourself lunch that strains an intern stipend. One tier over budget, minus a star.
elimination.downtown_indigo_arch: $ and vegetarian-friendly, but slow coursed service; reviewer was late back to the office. Misses the quick-lunch preference, minus a star.
elimination.downtown_pepper_tree: Fast, cheap, has a black bean burger, but it is a burger place, not curry. Misses the craving, minus a star (and a repeat of the burger-day problem).
elimination.downtown_tamarind_lane: $, curry, three vegetarian curries as full plates, counter service with time to spare. Meets everything.

notes: Mina's vegetarianism is never stated, only implied through the burger-day and pepperoni callbacks plus her line about curries she 'can actually order'. That was fair and enjoyable to work out, but a player who skims could take it as picky eating rather than a strict diet. It doesn't change the pick here, since Copper Pot is the only venue that fails it and it would lose on 'a few curries i can actually order' anyway.
The budget is clear in tone but has no explicit tier. 'If it's pricey' together with the iced-tea complaint points to $, and Cardamom House's stipend review confirms $$ is too much.
The night-market noodle stall line is a red herring or setup for a later level. Maya dismisses it right away, so it is not a constraint.
Each decoy fails exactly one constraint, which makes the elimination clean. Nothing felt contradictory.
